title: Value constraints: support ranges and open-ended bounds (importer drops them)
description:
BUG + GAP (highest value). The metamodel's ValueConstraint is enumerated
values only -- Constraint.ts:81-88: `readonly values: readonly string[]`,
with the doc comment "Currently supports enumerated values."

Consequence in the importer: NormaXmlParser.ts:262 keeps a value range
ONLY when `minVal === maxVal`:

    if (minVal !== undefined && minVal === maxVal) { values.push(minVal); }

So every genuine ORM 2 value range -- `[1..10]`, `>= 18`, `(0..100)`,
mixed sets like `{1, 3, 5..9}` -- is **silently dropped on import**. Same
pattern at NormaXmlParser.ts:497-508 for role-level value constraints.

ORM 2 / NORMA value constraints support enumerations, closed ranges,
open/half-open ranges, and unions of these, with inclusive/exclusive
bounds. This is one of the most common conceptual constraints in real
models (ages, ratings, percentages, codes), so the loss is material.

Work: (a) extend ValueConstraint to a list of items where each item is a
literal OR a range with optional lower/upper bound and inclusivity flags;
(b) update NormaXmlParser to carry ranges through; (c) update validation
and verbalization; (d) round-trip fixture test. Keep `values: string[]`
working as a sugar/back-compat for pure enumerations.
acceptance_criteria: ValueConstraint can express inclusive/exclusive ranges, open-ended bounds, and mixed enumerations+ranges; NormaXmlParser imports MinValue!=MaxValue ranges and open bounds without loss; round-trip test over a NORMA value-range fixture; validation + verbalization handle ranges.
close_reason: Value ranges and open/exclusive bounds implemented: metamodel (ValueRange + ranges on ValueConstraint/ValueConstraintDef), serializer round-trip, JSON Schema, verbalization, population validation, and the NORMA importer (parser+mapper) which no longer drops MinValue!=MaxValue ranges. Tests added across core and formats; full monorepo build/test/lint green.

title: ORM 2 standard coverage audit: .orm.yaml/NORMA importer gaps
description:
Audit of conceptual ORM 2 coverage in the native `.orm.yaml` metamodel
(packages/core/src/model) and the NORMA XML importer
(packages/formats/src/Norma*), measured against the ORM 2 standard as
realized by NORMA. Goal: make barwise "play well with others" by closing
the genuine semantic divergences from NORMA before any export/round-trip
work.

Method: read each metamodel type and the NORMA parser/mapper, then
classify every candidate gap as REAL (file a child) or NOT-A-GAP
(already covered). Diagram/layout interop is intentionally out of scope
here (tracked separately by barwise-e3g) -- this epic is about *conceptual*
ORM 2 semantics only.

NOT gaps (verified covered, do not file):
- Preferred identifier: activated in NormaToOrmMapper.ts:375 (is_preferred).
- Unary/n-ary fact types: supported (FactType.ts:22-23, arity getter).
- Subtype partition (exclusive/exhaustive): SubtypeFact carries both flags.
- Implied mandatory constraints: intentionally filtered (NORMA auto-generated).
- Conceptual data types: 20+ NORMA types normalized to portable names.

REAL gaps (each a child of this epic):
1. Value ranges + open-ended value constraints (HIGH; also a silent
   import data-loss bug).
2. Derived fact types / derivation rules.
3. Deontic vs alethic constraint modality.
4. Object cardinality constraints (distinct from role frequency).
5. Independent (reference-independent) object types.
6. Set-comparison/ring constraints over join paths.
7. Default values on value types / roles.
8. Multi-role (role-sequence) frequency constraints.

Children 1-2 are the priority. Once the gap list is agreed, the
follow-on work is (a) a NORMA-vs-yaml comparison doc and (b) a spec for
NORMA export / round-trip; both are tracked separately.
notes:
Authoritative XSD census (2026-06-17) against ormsolutions/NORMA ORMModel/ObjectModel/ORM2Core.xsd confirmed the original (import-grounded) audit and surfaced constructs the code-grounded pass could not see (elements the importer never references). New children .9-.13 added. Minor verbalization/metadata not separately filed: IsPersonal (pronoun hint), RecognizedPhrases (verbalization phrases), IsExternal (externally-defined elements). Note: ORM2Core models value constraints as ValueTypeValueRestriction/RoleValueRestriction (not a *Constraint), which the importer already handles -- not a gap.
Cited deep-research pass (2026-06-17) compared the ORM2 book (Halpin & Morgan 2008; Halpin papers) against NORMA. Conclusion: ORM2Core.xsd is a faithful, near-superset realization of the book -- the gaps vs the book are TOOLING-completeness, not schema, in two spots: deontic modality (single-operator only, see .3) and formal derivation rules (partial, see .2). Methodology (CSDP, schema transformations, Rmap) is algorithms over models, not metamodel constructs, so 'missing' does not apply. Corrections to earlier chat claims: 'deep support for conceptual outer joins' was UNVERIFIED (inner joins confirmed; retract); semiderived('+') is NOT derived-and-stored('**'). Using ORM2Core.xsd as the completeness yardstick for STATIC STRUCTURAL ORM2 (the exporter's subset) is sound.

title: Map diagnostics to YAML source positions instead of line 0
description: Currently DiagnosticsProvider hard-codes all diagnostic ranges to line 0, character 0, which causes yellow squiggly lines to appear under orm_version instead of the actual problematic objects/facts. The core Diagnostic objects include an elementId (UUID) but the provider ignores it. Fix requires: (1) YAML source mapping during deserialization so element IDs can be traced back to line/character positions, (2) DiagnosticsProvider to use elementId to look up the correct range, (3) fallback to document start for project-level diagnostics that don't target a specific element.

title: Mandate identifier fact types in extraction prompt
description: GPT-5 Mini skips explicit identifier fact types (e.g. 'Patient has MedicalRecordNumber') even when entities have reference_modes. This causes downstream constraint skips because constraints reference fact types that don't exist. The prompt must explicitly instruct: for every entity with a reference_mode, emit a binary fact type 'Entity has Value' with is_preferred:true uniqueness on the entity role, reverse uniqueness on the value role, and mandatory on the entity role. This is the single highest-impact improvement for extraction quality.
close_reason: Resolved in v0.2.1 prompt (PR #51). Identifier fact types now mandated; all three transcripts produce them correctly.

title: Ternary fact type uniqueness should span Order+Product roles
description: In 'Order contains Product in Quantity', the uniqueness constraint is only on the Order role, meaning each Order contains at most one thing total. The transcript says 'Each line in the order specifies a product and a quantity' -- uniqueness should span Order+Product roles (each Order-Product combination has at most one Quantity). The LLM is not correctly identifying composite uniqueness for ternary fact types.
close_reason: Fixed in v0.2.2 prompt. Mini now produces composite uniqueness on Order+Product roles in ternary fact type.

title: Missing reverse uniqueness on reference-mode fact types
description: Reference-mode fact types (e.g., 'Customer has CustomerId') only get uniqueness on the entity role but not on the value role. The second constraint (each CustomerId identifies at most one Customer) is needed to make the identifier a bijection. The LLM recognizes the constraint conceptually (see NOTE annotations) but emits a duplicate of the entity-side constraint instead of creating a value-side constraint. May be an LLM prompt issue or a parser mapping issue.
close_reason: Fixed in v0.2.2 prompt. All identifier fact types now have both entity-role and value-role uniqueness constraints.

title: Customer places Order: uniqueness on wrong role
description: In the order-management transcript extraction, 'Customer places Order' has uniqueness on the Customer role (each Customer places at most one Order) instead of the Order role (each Order is placed by at most one Customer). The transcript clearly states 'Every order belongs to exactly one customer, and customers can place multiple orders.' This is a semantic inversion error in LLM extraction. Investigate whether the extraction prompt needs clearer guidance on which role to constrain for many-to-one relationships.
close_reason: Fixed in v0.2.2 prompt. Customer places Order now has uniqueness on Order role (each Order placed by one Customer).

title: Duplicate is_preferred constraints on reference-mode fact types
description: LLM extraction produces duplicate internal_uniqueness constraints with is_preferred: true on the same role in reference-mode fact types (e.g., 'Customer has CustomerId' has two identical constraints on the entity role). The parser should deduplicate constraints with identical type, roles, and is_preferred flag. Observed in order-management.orm.yaml lines 104-111, 127-134, 150-157.
close_reason: Fixed in v0.2.2 prompt. No duplicate is_preferred constraints in any v0.2.2 outputs.

title: Rename helpers/ -> workspace/ in CLI and MCP (name the imperative shell)
description:
The helpers/ folders in cli and mcp are a junk-drawer name over what is really the package's imperative shell: the impure boundary that resolves a <source> (file path / inline YAML / project manifest) into the model(s) a command or tool runs against, feeding the functional (pure) core. Rename helpers/ -> workspace/ to name that architectural role.

Scope (settle leaf layout in the spec):
- workspace/ holds the source-resolution + file-I/O cluster: io.ts (loadModel, isProjectFile, writeOutput), projectLoader.ts (loadProject), domainModels.ts/resolve.ts (resolveDomainModels/resolveModels), and lineageIo.ts (provenance I/O -- also shell I/O).
- Rendering is NOT io and stays a separate concern: CLI format.ts (formatDiagnostics/Verbalizations) and MCP response.ts (boundedTextResult). Decide its home in the spec (render/ vs flatten).

Decision (resolved with owner): keep the ~30-line loadProject duplication across CLI and MCP rather than a shared @barwise/workspace package. The pure assembly already lives in core (assembleProject, projectFilePaths); the three shells genuinely differ at the boundary (path vs inline YAML vs open editor document), so a shared resolver would force one to bend its interface -- exactly what the DRY-secondary principle warns against.

Tripwire to revisit the shared-package option: a third near-identical loader appears (e.g. vscode grows project loading) OR the duplicated impure glue grows past trivial.

Blast radius: ~32 import sites in cli, ~19 in mcp. Mechanical. Spec-first per project convention. Land AFTER PR #237 merges (same dev branch).
acceptance_criteria: helpers/ renamed to workspace/ in cli and mcp; all import sites updated; full suite + lint green; spec written documenting the functional-core/imperative-shell decision and the rendering split.
notes: Refinement (2026-06-21): projectLoader.ts is byte-identical across cli/mcp (true duplication, unlike resolve.ts which genuinely diverges). Owner considered + rejected hoisting the loader orchestration into core behind an injected file-reader port -- declined to keep core strictly effect-free. Duplication stays; escalation remains a shared @barwise/workspace package outside core, never core/io.

title: Book-verify: read 3rd ed. serialization (JSON/YAML) coverage (CC5)
description: The 3rd ed. (2024) newly covers JSON/YAML/markup serialization of ORM models -- barwise's exact domain. Read it and check whether the book sanctions a serialization framing the native .orm.yaml should align to. See docs/book-verification-checklist.md CC5.
notes:
BOOK QUESTIONS (3rd ed., 2024) to answer from the serialization / data-file-format / NoSQL chapters. Each maps to a barwise .orm.yaml choice to verify. barwise format: root keys {orm_version, model}; model = {name, domain_context, note, object_types[], fact_types[] (constraints INLINE), subtype_facts[], objectified_fact_types[], populations[], definitions[], diagrams[]}; roles/object-types referenced by opaque id.
Q1 Does the book show a worked JSON and/or YAML serialization of an ORM model (not just relational DDL)? Which listings/figures?
Q2 CRUX: is that JSON/YAML the CONCEPTUAL ORM model serialized, or the PHYSICAL target schema for a document/NoSQL DB the model maps TO? Does the book keep conceptual vs physical separate (ours: .orm.yaml is conceptual; DDL is derived)?
Q3 Top-level structure: separate object-type and fact-type collections (like ours), or organized differently?
Q4 Constraints INLINE on the fact type, or in a separate id-referenced section (NORMA-style)? [our key anti-NORMA choice]
Q5 Keyed by opaque ids + id-refs (id graph, NORMA-style), or by names/readings as primary keys?
Q6 How are fact-type readings represented (placeholder templates like '{0} ... {1}'?)
Q7 Are sample populations (fact instances) in the same file as the schema, or separate (CSV for data)? [we embed populations]
Q8 Does the conceptual serialization include diagram/layout/presentation info, or keep it out? [we embed diagrams]
Q9 Any schema/format VERSION field (like our orm_version)?
Q10 Derivation rule serialized as text or formal expression? Join/set-comparison path serialized as root+roles+projection?
Q11 Does the book name a canonical ORM interchange format, or treat NORMA .orm XML as the standard? Is JSON/YAML offered as interchange or just illustration?

title: Value-comparison constraints (role-to-role value comparison)
description:
GAP (confirmed against ORM2Core.xsd: ValueComparisonConstraintType).
ORM 2 supports value-comparison constraints asserting an ordering
relationship between the values of two roles, e.g. "Employee.startDate <
Employee.endDate" or "Sale.price >= Sale.cost". Operators: <, <=, =, <>,
>=, >. This is distinct from ring constraints (which relate two roles
played by the same object type by instance identity, not value order).

Neither the metamodel nor the importer has any notion of it (grep for
ValueComparisonConstraint in packages/formats is empty), so NORMA models
using it lose the constraint silently. This was invisible to the original
import-grounded audit because the importer never references the element.

Work: add a value-comparison constraint kind (two role ids + operator);
import ValueComparisonConstraint; verbalize; validate against populations.
acceptance_criteria: Metamodel can express a value-comparison constraint between two roles with an operator (<, <=, =, <>, >=, >); importer reads ValueComparisonConstraint; verbalization renders it; not conflated with ring constraints.
notes: Core construct landed (PR pending): model (ValueComparisonConstraint + operator union + isValueComparison guard), serializer round-trip, JSON Schema branch, verbalization (operator phrases), population validation (numeric/lexical), diff key, and the one-time orm_version 1.0 -> 1.1 bump (CURRENT_ORM_VERSION + schema const + no-op forward migration) per ADR-0001. Scope: v1 compares two roles of the SAME fact type; join-path value comparison is deferred to the role-path model (barwise-0s8/5t9.10). NORMA importer/exporter mapping deferred to a follow-on (RT-B fidelity) -- NORMA's ValueComparisonConstraint operator enum needs XSD verification. Leaving open until the importer lands.

title: Object cardinality constraints (population size), distinct from role frequency
description:
GAP. barwise has FrequencyConstraint (Constraint.ts:216-231) which bounds
how many times an object plays a *role* ("each Customer places 2..5
Orders"). ORM 2 also has CARDINALITY constraints that bound the *number
of instances* of an object type (or the number of instances playing a
role): "there are at most 50 Departments", "between 2 and 10 active
Promotions". These are different concepts and NORMA models them
separately.

There is no way to express object-population cardinality today, so such
constraints are lost on import and unrepresentable in authored models.

Work: add a cardinality constraint kind keyed on an object type (and
optionally a role), with min/max (max may be unbounded); wire import,
verbalization, validation against populations.
acceptance_criteria: Metamodel can express a cardinality bound on an object type's population (and optionally on a role's instance count); importer reads NORMA CardinalityConstraint; verbalization renders it; not conflated with FrequencyConstraint.
notes: Core construct (WS1-WS3) implemented: shared CardinalityRange; ObjectType.cardinality field + unary CardinalityConstraint union member; round-trip + JSON Schema; population-gated validation (object-type count via buildObjectUniverse, unary-role count via valuesPlayedInRole; deontic -> warning); unary arity-1 structural check; verbalization (both forms); diff. WS4 NORMA mapping deferred -> see follow-up issue.

title: Derived fact types and derivation rules
description:
GAP. No derivation concept exists in the metamodel (rg for
deriv/derived across core/src/model returns only an unrelated comment in
SubtypeFact.ts). ORM 2 supports derived predicates -- purely derived
(computed on demand) and derived-and-stored -- each carrying a
derivation rule (formal/relational or natural-language). Subtype-defining
rules are the same family (a subtype defined by a predicate rather than
asserted).

Today every fact type in `.orm.yaml` is asserted/base; a modeler cannot
say "Person is an Adult iff Person has Age >= 18" or "TotalPrice is
derived from Quantity * UnitPrice." NORMA models that use derivation lose
that intent on import.

Work: add an optional derivation field to FactType (and a defining-rule
option to SubtypeFact), decide the rule representation (start with a
free-text/natural-language rule string + a derivation kind enum), wire
import where NORMA expresses it, and verbalize. Keep formal rule grammar
out of scope for v1.
acceptance_criteria: Metamodel can mark a fact type as derived (purely-derived or derived-and-stored) and attach a derivation rule; importer reads NORMA derivation rules where present; verbalization renders the rule; validation treats derived facts appropriately.
notes: Core construct (WS1-WS3) implemented: DerivationRule/DerivationKind/DerivationStorage; FactType.derivation + SubtypeFact.definingRule; round-trip + JSON Schema; derivation consistency validation (blank-rule warning, purely-derived-with-population warning); verbalization (fact-type derivation sentence + subtype defining-rule clause); diff (derivation change on fact types). Subtype-fact diffing does not exist in the codebase, so the spec's 'defining_rule into subtype diff' line is N/A (noted in PR). WS4 NORMA mapping deferred -> follow-up issue.

title: Deontic vs alethic constraint modality
description:
GAP. No modality concept exists (rg for deontic/alethic across
core/src/model returns nothing). ORM 2 distinguishes ALETHIC constraints
(logical necessity -- cannot be violated in any valid population, the
default) from DEONTIC constraints (obligation -- should hold, but
violations are recorded rather than impossible). NORMA renders these
differently (solid vs dashed/violet, "must/may" vs "should/should not").

Currently all barwise constraints are implicitly alethic, so deontic
business rules ("a manager should not approve their own expense") cannot
be expressed and are lost on import.

Work: add an optional `modality: "alethic" | "deontic"` to the shared
constraint shape (default alethic), thread it through import,
verbalization (modal verb selection), and validation (deontic violations
are warnings/recorded, not errors).
acceptance_criteria: Every constraint can carry a modality (alethic default | deontic); importer reads NORMA modality; verbalization uses the correct modal wording (must/may vs should/should not); default remains alethic for back-compat.
notes: Implemented: shared ConstraintBase carries modality?; serializer round-trips (deontic-only emission); JSON Schema enum on all branches; verbalization prefixes 'It is obligatory that'; deontic population violations are warnings via severityForModality; diff key folds modality. DEFERRED: NORMA Modality=Deontic import/export pending ORM2Core.xsd verification (same caution as other deferred NORMA mappings).

title: Symbolic model query API in @barwise/core
description:
Build a deterministic, programmatic query interface over the ORM metamodel. Treats the model as a queryable graph of object types, fact types, roles, and constraints.

This is foundational: it makes the @barwise chat agent cheaper and more trustworthy (most 'questions about the model' become structured queries, not LLM prompts), it gives derivation rules a target language ('a derivation rule is just a named query'), and it gives CLI/MCP a stable surface for model introspection.

Examples of questions it must answer deterministically:
- What fact types involve <object type>?
- What constraints reference <role>?
- What is downstream / upstream of objectifying this fact?
- What object types have no mandatory roles? (model-quality query)
- What fact types share roles with <fact type>?

Interface surface:
- @barwise/core: new public API (likely src/query/ alongside validation, verbalization)
- CLI: new 'barwise query' command, or extend 'barwise show' subcommands
- MCP: new query_model tool exposing the API
- VS Code: chat agent (@barwise) delegates to this API for deterministic questions before falling back to LLM
acceptance_criteria: Public API documented; CLI subcommand works; MCP tool registered; chat agent uses it for at least 5 representative deterministic queries

title: OWL/SHACL import/export connector
description:
Add a format connector for the W3C semantic-web stack: OWL for class hierarchies and property characteristics, SHACL for closed-world data validation.

Per discussion comparing conceptual modeling approaches: ORM2's constraint vocabulary maps closely to SHACL's, and ORM2 + SHACL is the strongest combination on the page that no current tool ships. This connector reframes Barwise from 'ORM2 tool' to 'fact-oriented front-end to the W3C stack'.

Plugs into the existing FormatDescriptor registry in @barwise/core (packages/core/src/format/).

Interface surface:
- CLI: 'barwise export --format=owl|shacl', 'barwise import --format=owl'
- MCP: existing export_model / import_model tools pick up the new format automatically via the registry
- VS Code: register format in import/export commands and quick-pick

Mapping notes:
- ORM uniqueness -> sh:unique
- ORM mandatory / cardinality -> sh:minCount / sh:maxCount / owl cardinality restrictions
- ORM ring constraints -> owl property characteristics (subset) + SHACL-SPARQL for the rest
- ORM subtypes -> rdfs:subClassOf / owl:disjointWith
- ORM objectified facts -> intermediate resource pattern
acceptance_criteria: OWL+SHACL output validates with pySHACL; round-trip preserves ORM constraints that have direct OWL/SHACL analogs; CLI, MCP, and VS Code can all use the format

title: Analyze @barwise/core: stronger functional design and a domain-faithful type system
description:
An analysis pass over @barwise/core (findings + recommendations, not a refactor) along two intertwined axes.

1. Functional design. Survey how functional the core actually is and where it can go further: confirm the deterministic capabilities (validation, verbalization, mapping, diff, query, serialization) are genuinely pure -- same input, same output, no fs/network/clock/randomness and no injected effect ports. Look for hidden mutation, shared mutable state, or effectful seams that crept in. Identify where immutability, total functions (no partial/throwing paths that could be encoded in the return type), and pure transformation pipelines would strengthen the core. The standing commitment from barwise-e8m holds: core stays clean and functional.

2. Domain-faithful, strongly typed core. Review how the TypeScript types model the ORM 2 / Object-Role Modeling domain and how clearly they reflect it. Goal: a strongly typed core whose types ARE the domain model -- a reader should learn ORM from the types. Look at:
   - Making illegal states unrepresentable (discriminated unions over the metamodel element kinds; exhaustive switches the compiler enforces).
   - Precise nominal/branded types for identifiers and references (e.g. distinct id types per element kind) instead of bare string.
   - Tightening loose spots (string unions vs enums, optional fields that encode invariants, any/unknown leakage at boundaries, over-wide config types vs constructed domain types).
   - Whether the serialized .orm.yaml config shapes and the in-memory domain types are cleanly separated (parse-into-domain at the edge, domain types in the interior).
   - Parse-don't-validate framing: push validation into type construction so downstream core code receives already-valid domain values.

The two axes reinforce each other: a stronger type system makes the functional core safer and more self-documenting, and a pure core makes precise types tractable.

Output: a findings doc enumerating concrete opportunities, each tied to a core principle, ranked by payoff vs blast radius. Relates to barwise-e8m (functional-core tension discussion) and barwise-5d7 (imperative-shell boundary).
acceptance_criteria: A written findings/recommendations doc covering (a) functional-purity opportunities and (b) type-system/domain-modeling opportunities in @barwise/core, each tied to a design principle and ranked by payoff vs blast radius. Analysis only -- no behavior change and no refactor landed by this issue.

title: Standing discussion: shell duplication vs a clean functional core
description:
Capture and think through the standing tension between two of our principles in the imperative-shell area, without prescribing a fix.

The tension: DRY (secondary) vs a clean functional core (primary). projectLoader.ts is byte-identical across cli and mcp -- real duplication of project-assembly orchestration that is conceptually pure core logic, stranded in the shells only by an embedded readFileSync. The obvious dedup moves (a shared resolver, or hoisting the orchestration into core behind an injected file-reader port) each pull against keeping core strictly effect-free. We have deliberately chosen, for now, to live with the duplication rather than compromise the core.

This issue is a place to keep discussing that trade-off as the code evolves -- what we are observing, where the duplication is actually costing us, and how a stronger functional core would reshape the boundary -- NOT to land a specific solution. The one fixed commitment is that the core stays clean and functional (no side effects, no injected effect ports); everything else about how we resolve the shell duplication is open and exploratory.

Relates to barwise-5d7 (imperative-shell naming) and the memory cli-mcp-helpers-folders-are-the-imperative-shell.
acceptance_criteria: An evolving written discussion of the tension (kept current as we learn more), anchored on the one commitment to a clean functional core. No solution prescribed and no behavior change required by this issue.

ORM 2 has a general ROLE-PATH model: a path starts at a root object type
and traverses roles across fact types, joining on shared object types,
with object unifiers merging path nodes. This substrate underlies three
things barwise lacks: join-path set-comparison/ring constraints (5t9.6),
derivation rule paths (5t9.2), and modeler-defined queries (sibling
issue). The flat role-id sequences barwise uses today cannot express it.

Work (spec-first; larger design): design the role-path representation and
its serialization, then layer the dependents on it. 5t9.6 depends on this.
acceptance_criteria: A role-path representation (lead role path from a root object type, sub-paths, joins on shared object types, object unifiers) usable by set-comparison constraints, derivation rules, and queries; importer reads LeadRolePath/JoinRule/ObjectUnifier.
notes: PR (revised representation) implemented per the canonical-research finding: JoinOperand = RolePath + projection (node indices); join_subset/equality/exclusion compare projected tuple SETS (Halpin's role-sequence-projected-from-a-join-path), not single endpoints. Updated model/serde/schema (join_operand_def)/structural validation (projection range, arity + column-type agreement)/tuple-set population evaluation/verbalization/diff. Single-column is projection length 1; PR-1's endpoint behavior is the [root,endpoint] special case. NORMA substrate (purpose tags, RolePathOwner, calculated projections) intentionally not copied.

title: Multi-role (role-sequence) frequency constraints
description:
GAP (minor). FrequencyConstraint binds a single role
(Constraint.ts:227 `readonly roleId: string`). ORM 2 frequency
constraints can range over a role SEQUENCE (a combination of roles), e.g.
"each (Room, TimeSlot) combination is booked 0..1 times". Multi-role
NORMA frequency constraints can't be represented and are dropped/narrowed.

Work: allow FrequencyConstraint to take a role-id sequence (keep single
-role as the common case); update import, verbalization, validation.
acceptance_criteria: FrequencyConstraint can span a role sequence, not just a single role; importer maps NORMA multi-role FrequencyConstraint; verbalization handles it.
close_reason: Implemented: FrequencyConstraint.roleId -> roleIds (role sequence); back-compat serialization (role/roles); per-tuple validation; multi-role verbalization; diff; NORMA multi-role round-trip included. Tier 2 complete.

title: Set-comparison and ring constraints over join paths
description:
GAP (advanced). barwise's set-comparison constraints reference flat role
-id sequences (SubsetConstraint.subsetRoles/supersetRoles,
EqualityConstraint, ExclusionConstraint). There is no join-path concept
(rg join/role-path/rolepath in core/src/model finds nothing relevant).

ORM 2 allows these constraints to range over JOIN PATHS -- role sequences
that traverse several fact types joined on shared object types (e.g. a
subset constraint between a path A-plays-B-in-FT1 and B-relates-C-in-FT2).
NORMA persists these as multi-fact RoleSequences with join semantics.
Without a join-path model, such constraints can't round-trip and complex
NORMA models lose them.

Work: design a join-path representation (ordered hops over fact types,
joined on object types) usable by subset/equality/exclusion/ring; parse
NORMA's joined RoleSequences. Larger design effort -- spec first.
acceptance_criteria: Subset/equality/exclusion (and ring) constraints can reference role sequences defined over a join path spanning multiple fact types; importer reads NORMA join-path role sequences; documented limitations for v1.
notes: XSD: set-comparison constraints use ConstraintRoleSequenceWithJoinType over the role-path model (LeadRolePath/JoinRule/ObjectUnifier). This is an instance of the general role-path substrate filed as .13; .6 depends on .13.

title: Default values on value types and roles
description:
GAP (minor). No default-value concept (rg default in Role.ts/ObjectType.ts
finds nothing). NORMA/ORM 2 allow a default value on a value type or a
role. Useful for relational mapping (SQL DEFAULT) and lost on import.

Work: optional `defaultValue?: string` on ObjectType (value types) and/or
Role; import from NORMA; thread into DDL rendering.
acceptance_criteria: Value types/roles can carry a default value; importer reads NORMA default values; relational mapping can emit DEFAULT where applicable.
notes: Implemented (PR pending): ObjectType.defaultValue (value-type default) + config + getter; serializer round-trip (default_value, emitted when present); JSON Schema property; and the DDL payoff -- Column.defaultValue, threaded by the relational mapper from the value type onto its column, rendered as SQL DEFAULT (numeric/boolean bare, else quoted with '' escaping). No orm_version bump (1.1 open). Deferred: NORMA import/export of DefaultValue -- NORMA's exact DefaultValue representation (attribute vs element, InvariantDefaultValue) needs XSD verification, like value-comparison's operator enum; folded into the NORMA-mapping follow-on. Role-level defaults also deferred (value-type default is the common/DDL-relevant case).

title: Independent (reference-independent) object types
description:
GAP. ObjectType has no `independent` flag (rg independent in
ObjectType.ts finds only an unrelated data-type comment). In ORM 2 an
INDEPENDENT object type (drawn with an open dot) may have instances that
participate in no fact other than its own reference -- i.e. it is not
existentially dependent on playing any asserted role. This matters for
reference schemes and for correct mandatory-role inference.

Work: add optional `independent?: boolean` (default false) to ObjectType,
import NORMA's IsIndependent attribute, and surface it in
verbalization/diagram. Low effort, improves fidelity.
acceptance_criteria: ObjectType can be marked independent; importer reads NORMA's independent flag; verbalization/diagram note it; default false.
notes: Implemented (PR pending): ObjectType.independent (default false) + config; serializer round-trip (emitted only when true); JSON Schema property; completeness-warning exemption (independent types are not flagged 'isolated'); and the full NORMA round-trip -- parser reads IsIndependent, mapper maps it, writer+serializer emit IsIndependent (RT-A test). No orm_version bump (1.1 already open). Remaining: diagram open-dot marker for independent types is a @barwise/diagram follow-on (verbalization has no object-type-property slot today; the ADR 'verbalizable' gate is satisfied conceptually).

title: Verify R2RML/RML export status; build if missing
description:
Per discussion, R2RML (W3C standard for declaring how relational rows map to RDF triples) was thought to be on the roadmap or already implemented. But the current core/src/export/ directory only contains Avro, dbt, DDL, and OpenAPI exporters — no R2RML.

R2RML addresses the real-world scenario the W3C-stack section of the comparison doc names explicitly: relational database of record, but want to publish as ontology-backed graph. Pairs naturally with the OWL/SHACL connector (barwise-e8c) — together they cover the 'relational + RDF' workflow that ORM2 is uniquely positioned to drive from a single conceptual model.

Scope of THIS issue: investigate. If R2RML is genuinely missing, this issue converts into the build task. If it's somewhere I missed, close as resolved.

Interface surface (if built):
- CLI: 'barwise export --format=r2rml'
- MCP: existing export_model tool picks it up via FormatDescriptor registry
- VS Code: export commands
acceptance_criteria: Status confirmed (present/absent). If absent and we decide to build: R2RML output validates against a reference tool (Ontop or Morph-KGC); CLI/MCP/VS Code all expose it

title: Move web viewer mockup from Claude Designer into repo
description:
ORM2 scores 'None' on the Cloud/web tooling row of the conceptual-modeling-approaches matrix — NORMA is Visual Studio only. Barwise can close that gap with even a read-only web viewer: 'share this model with a stakeholder via a URL.'

A mockup exists in Claude Designer under a personal account. First step is to move it into this repo so it can be iterated on with everyone.

title: Add sample population to an example .orm.yaml file
description:
The ORM metamodel and serialization already support sample populations (instances populating fact types, validated against constraints in real time). Per discussion: this is one of the most stakeholder-friendly features. Combined with verbalization, populations are the killer demo — 'here's the rule in English, here's data that satisfies it, here's data that violates it.'

But no example .orm.yaml currently demonstrates populations. New users and reviewers don't see the feature exists.

Scope: pick an existing example (or add a new small one), add a sample population that exercises multiple constraint types — mandatory, uniqueness, value constraint, maybe a ring constraint. Make sure validation catches deliberate violations and lets correct rows pass.

Interface surface:
- Examples/docs only — no code interface change
- But: VS Code population validation UI, CLI 'barwise validate', and MCP 'validate_model' should all light up usefully when run on the example
acceptance_criteria: Example .orm.yaml includes a populated section; running validation surfaces both passes and intentional failures; example is referenced from docs/README

title: LLM-assisted derivation rule elicitation (English to formal rule)
description:
ORM2 derivation rules define a fact type whose population is computed from other fact types (e.g., 'Person is a Senior Citizen if Person has Age > 65'). FORML (ORM's textual rule language) is limited and academically oriented.

Two complementary pieces:
1. A formal rule language as a target: likely Datalog-style over the metamodel, leveraging the symbolic query API (barwise-6i6). 'A derivation rule is a named query.'
2. LLM-assisted elicitation: user describes a rule in English; LLM translates to the formal language; user reviews and saves. Mirrors how verbalization works in the other direction.

Key principle: LLM is a translator, NOT a reasoner. The rule itself is formal and executable; the LLM just helps author it.

Interface surface:
- @barwise/core: rule language parser + evaluator (built on query API)
- CLI: 'barwise rule add' / 'barwise rule list' / 'barwise rule eval'
- MCP: 'propose_rule' tool (LLM-assisted authoring) + 'evaluate_rule' tool (execution)
- VS Code: chat agent supports 'add a derivation rule that...' workflow; rules editor in webview

Depends on barwise-6i6 (symbolic query API).
acceptance_criteria: Formal rule language documented; round-trip English -> rule -> verbalization works; evaluator produces correct derivations on test models; all three interfaces support the workflow

title: Strengthen @barwise chat to delegate deterministic questions to symbolic query API
description:
The @barwise VS Code chat agent currently answers questions about ORM models primarily via LLM prompting. For deterministic questions (what fact types involve X, what constraints reference role Y, etc.) this is wasteful and untrustworthy. The agent should delegate these to the symbolic model query API (barwise-6i6) before falling back to LLM reasoning.

Two distinct concerns to separate:
- Symbolic Q&A over the model — deterministic, no LLM needed (use query API)
- Inferred entailments, natural-language synthesis, ambiguity resolution — LLM appropriate

Pattern: the chat agent receives a question, attempts to classify it as symbolic vs reasoning, calls the appropriate path. LLM still does English-to-query translation and result narration.

Interface surface:
- VS Code: @barwise chat participant — primary consumer
- MCP: the same delegation logic should be exposed so external agents (not just VS Code) get the same benefit
- CLI: less direct, but 'barwise query' subcommand gives the same surface for scripting

Depends on barwise-6i6 (symbolic model query API).
acceptance_criteria: At least 5 representative deterministic questions answered without LLM call; chat agent transcripts show clear delegation; same behavior available via MCP

title: Reference ontology import connectors (schema.org, FIBO, QUDT)
description:
Add import connectors for well-known reference ontologies so modelers can pull in standard vocabularies rather than re-defining concepts. This addresses the 'no IRI / no linked-data' gap in ORM2 by anchoring object types and value types to external definitions.

Likely an epic with one connector per vocabulary:
- schema.org (general purpose, very broad)
- FIBO (financial industry business ontology)
- QUDT (units / quantities / dimensions)
- Possibly others (DCAT for data catalogs, FOAF, etc.)

Plugs into the FormatDescriptor registry.

Interface surface:
- CLI: 'barwise import --format=schema-org --filter=<...>' or 'barwise reference add <iri>'
- MCP: import_model tool, or a new reference_lookup tool
- VS Code: a 'browse reference ontologies' UI or command palette entry

Open design questions:
- Do we materialize imports into the .orm.yaml, or maintain references to external IRIs?
- How does this interact with our (currently absent) IRI support on object types?
acceptance_criteria: At least schema.org import works end-to-end; modeler can anchor an ORM object type to a referenced concept; CLI/MCP/VS Code all support the workflow

title: Property Graph Schema (PG-Schema) export connector
description:
Add a format connector for PG-Schema (LDBC, 2023) and/or Neo4j Cypher schema. Property graphs are the increasingly common 'I want a graph but OWL is too much' middle ground, and ORM2's attribute-free nature is a near-perfect source for property graphs.

Plugs into the FormatDescriptor registry in @barwise/core.

Interface surface:
- CLI: 'barwise export --format=pg-schema' (and possibly --format=cypher)
- MCP: existing export_model tool picks it up via the registry
- VS Code: register in export commands

Mapping notes:
- ORM object types -> node labels
- ORM binary fact types -> relationship types (or properties on nodes for single-valued)
- ORM objectified facts -> intermediate nodes
- ORM uniqueness / mandatory -> PG-Schema key / cardinality constraints
acceptance_criteria: PG-Schema output parses with a reference validator; CLI/MCP/VS Code can all invoke export

title: Write 'Splitting a model into an OrmProject' guide
description: Write a user-facing guide under docs/ that walks through converting a monolithic .orm.yaml into a multi-file OrmProject. The conceptual treatment in ARCHITECTURE.md §3.1.4 covers the metamodel but not the workflow. The guide should use auction.orm.yaml as the worked example, splitting it into catalog/auctions/payments/parties domains with context mappings between them. Cover: when to split (signals you've outgrown a single file), how to identify bounded contexts, the .orm-project.yaml manifest, .map.yaml for cross-context entity mappings, the 'context:ObjectType' qualified-ref syntax, and how to load/validate/diagram the result. Cross-link from docs/CLI.md, docs/MCP.md, and examples/README.md.
acceptance_criteria: docs/ORM_PROJECT_GUIDE.md (or similar) exists with a worked auction.orm.yaml split example; CLI.md/MCP.md/examples/README.md link to it; a new reader can follow the steps and end up with a working multi-domain project.

title: CLI tooling to scaffold an OrmProject from a monolithic model
description: Add CLI commands to make project scaffolding ergonomic. Today converting auction.orm.yaml into a multi-domain project means hand-editing YAML and cutting entities across files — error-prone and tedious. Proposed commands: (a) 'barwise project init <name>' creates a new empty .orm-project.yaml with the standard directory layout, (b) 'barwise project split <source.orm.yaml> --domains catalog,auctions,payments' interactively or by config assigns entities/facts to domains and writes the resulting files plus suggested context mappings for any entity referenced across seams. The split command should produce a valid project on output (round-trip loads cleanly) and flag entities that need manual resolution (multiple seams, ambiguous ownership).
design: Start with 'barwise project init' (trivial). For 'split', start with a config-driven mode: user supplies a YAML file mapping entity IDs to domain names, tool does the cut. Interactive/LLM-assisted modes can follow later.
acceptance_criteria: 'barwise project init' produces a valid empty project; 'barwise project split' with a config file cuts auction.orm.yaml into the 4 subdomains from the discussion and the output loads, validates, and diagrams cleanly.

title: Subdomain categorization for entities and fact types
description:
## Problem

An ORM model has a single top-level 'domain_context' string, but individual
entity types and fact types have no way to be tagged by subdomain. In a
realistic model, many entities naturally belong to sub-domains like
'transaction', 'catalog', 'customer', 'fulfillment', etc. Users need a way
to understand which parts of a model belong to which subdomain, filter
by subdomain, and answer questions like "show me everything in the
transaction domain."

## Current state

- 'OrmModel.domainContext' is a single string on the whole model
- 'ObjectType' and 'FactType' have no domain/category/tag fields
- 'OrmProject' supports multi-file models where each file has its own
  'domain_context' — that covers cross-file separation but not within-file
  subdomains
- 'DiagramLayout' can define named visual views that subset the model,
  but those are visual groupings, not semantic domain tags
- 'describeDomain' tool operates on the whole model; it does not filter
  by subdomain

## Design space to explore

1. **Explicit domain tags** — add an optional 'domain' (or 'domains: string[]')
   field to ObjectType and FactType. Simple, explicit, but puts the burden
   on the modeler to tag things consistently.
2. **Named subdomains as first-class elements** — a top-level 'subdomains'
   list, each naming a set of entity/fact type IDs. Benefits: supports
   overlapping subdomains, displayable in the sidebar, can be used for
   filtering and scoped exports.
3. **Derived clustering** — infer subdomains automatically from graph
   structure (connected components, louvain community detection, shared
   fact types). No modeler burden, but fuzzy and may not match intent.
4. **Namespace-prefixed names** — e.g. 'Transaction.Payment' → derived
   from naming convention. Discourages good naming practice.
5. **Hybrid** — first-class subdomains (option 2) with LLM-assisted
   suggestion of subdomain membership from the model structure + names.

## Downstream uses

- Sidebar: group entities/facts by subdomain
- Diagram: filter to a single subdomain (similar to named views)
- describeDomain: filter by subdomain
- Export (DDL, OpenAPI): scoped export of a subdomain
- Impact analysis: "changes to X affect which subdomains"
- LLM context: when merging incoming changes, group related elements
  by subdomain for clearer diffs and verbalizations

## Not yet decided

- Should subdomains be hierarchical (Transaction > Payment > Refund)?
- Can an entity belong to multiple subdomains? (Probably yes.)
- How do subdomains interact with the existing 'OrmProject' multi-file
  domain_context — are they nested, parallel, or the same thing?
- Is this a core metamodel change (breaks serialization) or an
  annotation layer?

## Acceptance criteria

This issue is scoping/design only. A follow-up implementation issue
will be filed once the design direction is chosen. Success here means:

- [ ] ADR-style document capturing the chosen design (under docs/)
- [ ] Serialization impact assessed (round-trip, migration path)
- [ ] Impact on downstream consumers documented (sidebar, diagram,
      describeDomain, exports)

title: Expose sidebar/diagram interactions as LLM-accessible tools
description: The sidebar and diagram now support click-to-highlight, orientation toggle, position save, and model browsing. These same capabilities should be available to LLMs via the MCP server and Copilot chat tools so that an AI assistant can navigate, highlight, and manipulate diagrams programmatically. Examples: 'highlight Customer and its connections', 'save the current diagram layout', 'list all fact types for Order'. Bridges the gap between UI-driven and conversational workflows.

title: dbt source/staging YAML generation from diagram view
description: Generate dbt source and staging model YAML from a view's entities. Column names, data types, and descriptions come from the ORM model's entity types, fact types, and definitions. Bridges conceptual modeling directly into the analytics engineering workflow.

title: Data dictionary export from diagram view
description: Generate a human-readable data dictionary document from a view's elements. Lists entities with definitions, fact type readings, constraints, and data types. Output as Markdown or HTML. Useful for stakeholder review and documentation deliverables.

title: Scoped OpenAPI export from diagram view
description: Export OpenAPI schema for only the entities in the active view. Uses the existing OpenAPI format support scoped to the view's element subset.

title: Scoped DDL export from diagram view
description: Export DDL (CREATE TABLE statements) for only the entities in the active view, not the full model. Uses the existing relational mapping engine scoped to the view's element subset.

title: View switching in sidebar
description: Extend the sidebar model browser to show named views. Click a view to open it in the diagram panel. Active view highlighted. Add/remove elements from views via right-click context menu.

title: Named diagram views with element subsets
description: Support multiple named views per model, each containing a subset of elements. Create views from: subtype tree of an entity, N-degree neighborhood, or manual selection. Auto-include fact types that connect included entities so views are structurally complete. Store view definitions in the diagrams section of .orm.yaml.
close_reason: Implemented named diagram views with element subsets. Save View button in hop bar captures current filtered elements. Views stored in .orm.yaml with element names. Clicking a saved view in the sidebar loads it. Auto-includes connecting fact types and subtype facts.

title: Multi-view diagrams with submodel export
description: Support multiple named diagram views per .orm.yaml model, each containing a subset of elements with persisted positions. Views serve as scoped lenses (e.g., a report's data requirements, a type hierarchy). Key capabilities: (1) diagrams section in .orm.yaml schema, (2) sidebar tree view for navigation, (3) add/remove elements from views, (4) auto-include connecting fact types, (5) export a view's submodel as DDL, OpenAPI, or data dictionary. Inspired by NORMA's multi-diagram support (ormDiagram:ORMDiagram sections with per-shape AbsoluteBounds). Analytic use case: model known data domains, create views scoped to reports/deliverables, identify structural gaps, export scoped artifacts.

title: LLM transcript import: emit candidate constraints with TODO annotations
description: The LLM transcript extraction currently produces fact types without constraints, even when the transcript contains clear signals like 'exactly one', 'at most one', 'identified by', etc. The LLM should infer likely uniqueness and mandatory constraints from these phrases and emit them with TODO/NOTE annotations (similar to how it already annotates ambiguous identifiers) so the modeler can confirm, adjust, or remove them. This reduces the manual work needed after import while keeping the human in the loop.

title: Verbalization on entity selection
description: When an entity type is clicked in the diagram webview, display verbalizations of its fact types in a tooltip or side panel. Reuses click handler infrastructure from the focus subset feature. Requires integration with the verbalization engine from @barwise/core.

title: Extract objectified fact types from transcripts
description: The metamodel supports objectified fact types (a fact type that is also treated as an entity type, e.g. 'Enrollment' objectifying 'Student enrolls in CourseOffering'). The extraction prompt and DraftModelParser do not handle objectification. The LLM could be instructed to identify when a relationship is itself referenced as an entity in other fact types.

title: Extract frequency constraints from transcripts
description: The metamodel supports frequency constraints ('each X plays this role at least N / at most M times', e.g. 'each Employee works on at least 1 and at most 3 Projects'). Not handled in extraction.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #57

title: Extract ring constraints from transcripts
description: The metamodel supports ring constraints (irreflexive, asymmetric, intransitive, acyclic, etc. on self-referencing fact types, e.g. 'a Person cannot manage themselves' or 'the reports-to hierarchy must be acyclic'). Not handled in extraction.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #57

title: Extract equality constraints from transcripts
description: The metamodel supports equality constraints (two role populations are equal, e.g. 'a Person teaches a Course if and only if that Person is qualified for that Course'). Not handled in extraction.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #57

title: Extract subset constraints from transcripts
description: The metamodel supports subset constraints (one role population is a subset of another, e.g. 'every Person who manages a Department must also work in that Department'). Not handled in extraction.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #57

title: Extract exclusive-or constraints from transcripts
description: The metamodel supports exclusive_or (exactly one of several roles must be played -- combines disjunctive mandatory + exclusion, e.g. 'every Payment is exactly one of CashPayment, CardPayment, or CheckPayment'). Not handled in extraction.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #57

title: Extract exclusion constraints from transcripts
description: The metamodel supports exclusion constraints (two role combinations cannot both occur, e.g. 'a Person cannot be both a Student and an Instructor in the same Department'). Not handled in extraction prompt, ExtractionTypes, or DraftModelParser.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #57

title: Extract disjunctive mandatory constraints from transcripts
description: The metamodel supports disjunctive_mandatory (at least one of several roles must be played, e.g. 'every Person must have either a Phone or an Email'). Not handled in extraction prompt, ExtractionTypes, or DraftModelParser.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #57

title: Extract external uniqueness constraints from transcripts
description: The metamodel supports external_uniqueness (uniqueness spanning roles across multiple fact types, e.g. composite identification of CourseOffering by Course+Semester). The extraction prompt and DraftModelParser do not handle this constraint type. ExtractionTypes.ts InferredConstraintType only allows internal_uniqueness | mandatory | value_constraint.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #57

The TODO is stale/incorrect -- the annotator should not emit it when the constraint was handled at the value-type level.

The constraint matcher should recognize common patterns (e.g., role names matching object type names) to reduce noise. The positional fallback itself works fine but the volume of notes drowns out important annotations.

title: Add validation warnings for dataType and isPreferred consistency
description:
Add two completeness/consistency validation rules:

1. Warn when a value type has no dataType set. Value types should ideally declare their conceptual data type so the relational mapper can generate accurate column types instead of defaulting to TEXT.

2. Warn when an entity type has zero isPreferred uniqueness constraints (no preferred identifier declared) or more than one isPreferred constraint (conflicting preferred identifiers). This helps catch modeling issues early.

These are non-blocking warnings (not errors) in the validation engine, similar to existing completeness warnings in src/validation/rules/completenessWarnings.ts.

- tests/validation/completenessWarnings.test.ts

title: Add @orm Copilot Chat participant for guided domain elicitation
description:
Implement a VS Code Chat Participant (@orm) that guides users through structured ORM domain elicitation directly in the Copilot Chat panel.

The participant would:
- Walk users through a structured interview (identify entities, reference modes, relationships, cardinality, constraints, value restrictions)
- Build the ORM model incrementally with feedback at each step
- Use the existing LLM extraction pipeline from @BARWISE/llm
- Generate the .orm.yaml file when the conversation is complete
- Solve both the 'what questions to ask' and 'import the result' problems in a single interaction

This is more impactful than a static conversation guide because it lives where engineers already work (Copilot Chat panel), provides real-time guidance, and doesn't require a separate transcript import step.

Requires the VS Code Chat Participant API (vscode.chat.createChatParticipant).

title: OSI (Open Semantic Interchange) interoperability
description: Treat the Open Semantic Interchange (OSI) ontology spec as an interop target for barwise. OSI (github.com/open-semantic-interchange/OSI, Apache-2.0, spec v0.2.0.dev0) is an emerging vendor-agnostic semantic-interchange standard (YAML+JSON) with reference converters for dbt, GoodData, Polaris, and Salesforce. It is ORM-rooted and overlaps heavily with the barwise metamodel (EntityType/ValueType, roles, verbalizes patterns, identify_by preferred identifiers, built-in datatypes). This epic groups the work to interoperate with OSI and to close two capability gaps it surfaced (derivation expressions; logical-schema ingestion).
notes: Source: comparison performed 2026-06-23 against the raw OSI ontology spec. barwise remains richer on the ORM 2 constraint taxonomy (ring/exclusion/exclusive-or/subset/equality/frequency) and on DDD bounded-context mapping / data products; no action needed there.

title: OSI import/export format adapter
description: Add an 'osi' FormatDescriptor (importer + exporter) to the format registry so barwise can read and write OSI ontology files. Reuse existing plumbing: barwise/packages/core/src/format/types.ts (FormatDescriptor), formats.ts (registration), registry.ts. Mapping: OSI concept -> ObjectType (EntityType/ValueType -> kind); relationships -> FactType/Role; identify_by -> preferred identifier; multiplicity (ManyToOne/OneToOne) -> internal uniqueness + mandatory; verbalizes -> ReadingOrder; requires -> value/role constraints; extends -> SubtypeFact; built-in datatypes -> value types.
design: Key reshaping concern: OSI is concept-centric (relationships nested under the concept that plays the first role, OO dot-notation), whereas barwise keeps fact types as top-level fact-centric elements. The adapter must lift nested OSI relationships into standalone FactTypes on import and re-nest on export. Spec-first per repo conventions. derived_by and full requires-expression fidelity depend on the derivation-expression work (sibling issue) -- scope v1 to structural concepts/relationships/constraints and round-trip what maps cleanly.
acceptance_criteria: Round-trip an OSI example (e.g. the TPC-DS sample under OSI examples/) through import then export with no structural loss for supported constructs; unit tests in packages/core covering the concept/relationship/identifier/multiplicity/verbalization mappings.

title: Derivation expression language for derived fact types/concepts
description: Design a deterministic expression layer (parser + evaluator) in @barwise/core covering OSI derived_by semantics: dot-notation role navigation, boolean/comparison/aggregation operators, and recursion. OSI uses derived_by on both concepts (e.g. EXISTS(Person.earns)) and relationships (e.g. Person.parent_of(descendant) OR Person.ancestor_of.parent_of(descendant)). barwise currently has no formal expression language for derived fact types -- only prose definitions.
design: Must preserve the core determinism principle: same input, same output, no I/O. Core-only (no llm/cli deps). Spec-first. Enables higher-fidelity OSI round-trip and barwise-native derived metrics for data products (see ARCHITECTURE.md 3.1.5).

title: Logical-schema to model mapping (reverse Rmap / DB ingestion)
description: Add generic mapping from a logical/SQL schema into an OrmModel, analogous to OSI concept_mappings: object_mappings (SQL expressions populating concept instances), referent_mappings (resolving compound/entity identity through identifier relationships), and link_mappings (tree-structured patterns mapping logical data to relationship links at varying arities). Complements the existing forward Rmap in barwise/packages/core/src/mapping/ (ORM -> relational DDL) and the NORMA XML importer, which are currently the only ingestion paths.
design: OSI's mapping direction is logical-schema UP into the ontology -- the inverse of Rmap. This is the bridge that lets barwise consume existing warehouse schemas. Likely lands as an importer in the format/import layer rather than core/mapping. Spec-first.

title: ADR: OSI vs barwise comparison and interop strategy
description: Record an Architecture Decision Record under barwise/docs/decisions/ capturing the OSI-vs-barwise comparison and the decision to treat OSI as an interoperability format (import/export via the FormatDescriptor registry) rather than a metamodel replacement. Summarize the verified overlaps (EntityType/ValueType, roles, verbalization, preferred identifiers, built-in datatypes) and the divergences (OSI concept-centric organization, first-class derivation expressions, logical-schema-up mapping; barwise richer ORM 2 constraints and DDD bounded-context/data-product modeling).

title: spec-writer: fold barwise domain modeling into the spec flow
description:
Prototype: the spec-writer flow gains an optional 'model the domain' step -- when a spec introduces or reshapes a domain (new artifact kinds, file formats, persistent records, schema changes), author a companion .orm.yaml of the core domain, validated in CI (examples/models/ is already globbed by validate:examples).

Proven by the learning-design spec (PR #265): examples/models/learning-design.orm.yaml encodes C1 as a mandatory functional ternary, the catalog as 'each ReductiveBias is caught by exactly one CheckKind', and C6's card anatomy as mandatory Diagnosis/ReadingReference roles -- making the missing-diagnosis-field class of spec bug structurally inexpressible. Verbalization doubles as the articulation skill's verbalization test made mechanical; constraints are sensemaking anchors made executable.

Scope to consider:
1. spec-writer SKILL.md: a workflow step and a design-gate item ('domain-shaped spec ships a CI-validated companion model'), with criteria for when a spec earns a model (domain reshaping: yes; pure code movement: usually no).
2. template.spec.md: a companion-model section stub.
3. Bug-revisit protocol: when a bug traces to a wrong domain assumption, evolve the ORM model first (barwise diff shows the semantic change), then the spec prose, then the code.
4. Further out: use @barwise/code-analysis importers to extract a model FROM the implementation and barwise diff it against the spec's model -- a real spec-vs-code conformance check, closing the 'have we satisfied the requirements' loop deterministically.

Origin: session discussion on PR #265; the model-as-machine-checkable-core framing is already in the spec's 'The standard, as a barwise model' section.

title: Ambiguity should carry a questions list, not just a description
description:
The extraction prompt asks the model to state the question behind each ambiguity. The schema has nowhere to put one, so whether you get a question is luck.

systemPrompt.ts:112 instructs: "For each ambiguity, describe the specific question that needs to be answered", and all eight review categories model that in their examples. But the type carries only `description` and `source_references`. The question, when asked at all, is prose buried in the description; ReasoningTrail.ts:45 reduces each ambiguity to a.description, so nothing downstream could find it even when it is there.

What that produces, from the recorded order-management payload: "Stakeholders use 'customer' (CRM) and 'client' (billing) to refer to what appears to be the same concept, but billing only considers someone a client once they have paid. This may require separate entity types or a subtype relationship." Detection is excellent -- a real overloaded term with two source references -- but it is an observation plus a modeling suggestion, and a modeler still has to derive what to ask. A different run of the same pipeline produced "The stakeholders should clarify whether MembershipId exists or if composite identification is intended", which is actionable. Nothing structural holds the extractor to the second form.

Proposal: add `questions: readonly string[]` to Ambiguity. A list, not a single string, because one fork routinely needs more than one thing settled -- the customer/client case raises both "are these one concept or two?" and "does 'client' status begin at first payment, making it a state rather than a type?", and either answer alone leaves the model underdetermined.

Why it matters: an ambiguity is an agenda item for the next working session. An observation is not actionable; a question is. It also unblocks measurement -- requires_ambiguity (PR #302) substring-matches the description, so it scores topic detection and cannot tell a sharp question from a vague note. With a declared questions list a check can assert questions are present and non-empty: structural, deterministic, no LLM judge, which the harness rejects on principle.

Blast radius: ExtractionTypes.ts, prompt/responseSchema.ts, the parse in ExtractionPrompt.ts:65-79, ReasoningTrail.ts, the MCP import formatter, the VS Code display, and every recorded fixture payload under packages/llm/tests/fixtures/ and packages/promptlab/tests/fixtures/responses/.

To decide in the spec: optional vs required in the response schema. Required is what actually enforces the behavior, but it changes the prompt contract, can shift extraction, and would need re-measuring through `barwise prompt eval` -- which needs an API key that is not yet configured. Optional avoids forcing a re-baseline and leaves existing fixtures valid.

Spec before code, per project convention. Related: docs/specs/eval-transcript-realism.spec.md, whose non-goals exclude scoring ambiguity prose quality because it needs a judge -- a structured questions list is the route that does not. Mirrored on GitHub as issue #303.

title: prompt eval folds failed runs into the mean as zeros
description:
A run that never reached the model is scored 0 and averaged in as if the model produced a terrible extraction. runSuite.ts:82 catches every exception into {error}, and the aggregation does runs.map((r) => r.score?.score ?? 0), so an auth failure, a rate limit, or a dropped connection is indistinguishable in the mean from a genuine bad score.

CONFIRMED IN THE FIRST REAL USE (2026-08-20). Four runs against claude-haiku-4-5 produced four history rows, three of them junk:
  12:23 - all seven cases 0.000 (total failure: key set but not exported)
  12:27 - order-management 0.907, other six 0.000 (partial failure)
  12:31 - all seven cases 0.000 (total failure)
  12:44 - all seven non-zero, mean 0.781 (mostly real)
The 12:27 row is the diagnostic one: order-management is first in the manifest and runSuite walks cases in declared order, so three calls succeeded and every subsequent call failed -- the shape of a rate limit, not of a bad model. And the 12:44 row is not clean either: university-enrollment shows mean 0.356 with worst 0.000, so at least one of its three runs scored a hard zero, and nothing in the record says whether that was a failed call or a genuine miss on the known-bimodal case.

Also worth noting from the same session: all four rows record artifactVersion 1.0.0, the default. No tuned variant was measured, and nothing in the output made that obvious at a glance.

RESOLUTION (agreed 2026-08-20): retry is the primary mechanism, but it does not replace the recording fix -- the two failure classes observed above need different handling.

1. Retry with exponential backoff for transient failures: 429, 5xx, timeouts, connection resets. This is what the 12:27 row needed.
2. Fail fast for terminal failures: 401/403 auth, 400 malformed request. Retrying a bad key just fails more slowly, which is what the 12:23 and 12:31 rows would have done.
3. Either way, a run that never produced a payload must not enter the mean as a zero. Exclude it, carry a failure count on CaseSummary and SuiteReport, and print it.
4. The history writer should refuse to record a run with any surviving failure, or record it with an explicit sample count and a failure count so a later reader can tell a partial run from a complete one. Refusing is simpler and safer.

A parse failure is a separate case and should stay a zero: the model answered, the answer was unusable, that is a real score. Only failures that produced no response at all are excluded.

Open question for the fix: where retry belongs. Putting it in runSuite keeps it scoped to the eval lane; putting it in the provider clients under @barwise/llm helps every caller including MCP and VS Code, but widens the blast radius and needs its own decision about defaults. Recommend runSuite first, since the eval lane is where an unattended sweep makes a failure expensive.

Closed: shipped earlier in this session. runSuite now separates a provider that never answered (excluded from the mean, counted as a failure) from a model that answered unusably (a real zero), with retry classification in run/retry.ts and appendRunHistory refusing an incomplete run unless forced.

title: CLI bin is not executable after a fresh clone, install, and build
description:
`npx barwise` fails with "Permission denied" on a fresh checkout. packages/cli build is plain `tsc`, which emits dist/index.js at mode 644, and there is no chmod step. npm sets the executable bit on bin targets during install, but dist/ is gitignored, so on a fresh clone the file does not exist at install time and npm has nothing to chmod. The documented sequence -- npm install && npm run build -- therefore reliably produces a bin that cannot be executed.

Workarounds today: `node packages/cli/dist/index.js ...`, which ignores the mode, or a manual chmod +x, or re-running npm install after the build.

Proposed: a postbuild step on @barwise/cli using node rather than the shell, so it works on Windows too:
  "postbuild": "node -e \"require('node:fs').chmodSync('dist/index.js', 0o755)\""

CI never caught this because the release workflow bundles through esbuild and invokes the bundle directly, never the bin symlink. Worth a check in the CLI test plan (test-plan/cli-checks.sh) so a regression is caught by the release gate.

RESOLVED 2026-08-20. Wider than filed: three built files carry a shebang and none got the bit. packages/cli/dist/index.js (tsc, the bin target that failed with Permission denied), and both esbuild bundles -- packages/cli/dist/bundle/index.cjs and packages/mcp/dist/bundle/index.cjs, the latter being the barwise-mcp bin -- whose own header comment says they are meant to run "directly, via the shebang".

Fixed where each file is produced: a postbuild script on @barwise/cli for the tsc output, and a chmodSync at the end of each esbuild.mjs. node's chmodSync rather than a shell chmod, so Windows is unaffected.

Guarded in test-plan/cli-checks.sh, which the release workflow runs as a gate. The check was verified to fail when the bit is removed (gate exits 1), not merely to pass when it is present.

Cost before the fix: two eval runs. Once as Permission denied on npx barwise, and once as a stale dist/ that silently ran the old harness and produced three history rows without sample counts.

title: Edge release displays a stale date, hiding that its assets are current
description:
The edge pre-release shows a publish date two weeks older than its actual build, so it reads as stale when the downloads are current.

Verified on 2026-08-20: all four assets (CLI bundle, MCP bundle, VSIX, SHA256SUMS) carry updated_at 2026-08-20T12:03:44Z, one minute after the #302 merge, and the release body records the real build commit ee35478. But published_at is frozen at 2026-08-07T11:46:23Z and target_commitish still points at 042657380e, a June commit. GitHub surfaces the stale fields.

Cause is deliberate and worth keeping: release.yml never moves the edge tag, because a moving tag makes every contributor's git pull fail with "would clobber existing tag". `gh release edit --draft=false` on an already-published release does not bump published_at.

Proposed: put the build commit and date in the release title, which is the most prominent field in the releases list, via one added flag on the gh release edit call already in the workflow:
  --title "Edge build (${GITHUB_SHA::7} - $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d))"

No tag movement, so the git pull hazard stays solved, and the listing stops claiming a two-week-old build.

RESOLVED 2026-08-20. The edge release title now carries the build commit and date: "Edge build <short-sha> (<YYYY-MM-DD>)". Set on both branches of the step -- the gh release edit path, which previously set no title at all and left the stale "Edge build (latest main)" in place, and the gh release create path.

The tag still never moves, so the git pull hazard that motivated the fixed tag stays solved, and published_at and target_commitish stay stale as before. The difference is that the releases list no longer shows only stale fields: the title is the most prominent thing on the page and now says when the assets were actually built.

Not runnable outside CI, so validated three ways short of a live run: the YAML parses and the step still triggers on push with a title on both branches; the run block passes bash -n; and the title expression was executed against this repo's HEAD, producing "Edge build 2354177 (2026-08-20)".

title: CLI has no review command, though MCP and VS Code both expose it
description:
reviewModel (packages/llm/src/review/reviewModel.ts:288) is registered as the MCP review_model tool and called from packages/vscode/src/mcp/ToolRegistration.ts:248. packages/cli/src contains no reference to it and cli.ts registers no review command, so a CLI user cannot review a model while users of either other surface can.

Found by the cross-surface matrix in docs/unwired-capability-audit-2026-08-20.md.

The work is small -- reviewModel takes an OrmModel and an LlmClient, both of which the CLI already constructs for `barwise import transcript`. `barwise review <file> [--focus ...]` mirroring the MCP tool's options is the obvious shape.

Needs a key to exercise, like every LLM surface. Decide alongside barwise-810 (merge): either the CLI gets both and the surfaces converge, or the divergence gets written down as deliberate. What should not persist is undocumented divergence, which is how the parity claim in CLAUDE.md survived unchallenged.

Closed by docs/specs/cli-surface-parity.spec.md. `barwise review <file>` ships with --focus, the same provider options as `import transcript`, and --format text|json.

The question this issue raised -- decide alongside merge, either the surfaces converge or the divergence gets written down -- was answered by doing both. Review now reaches all three surfaces.

One design call worth recording: review always exits 0 when the review completes, whatever it says. No --fail-on flag. The suggestions are model-generated advice, and a command that failed a build on them would put an LLM in the merge path, where a bad day for the provider becomes a red build for everyone. A user who wants a gate pipes --format json through jq, which keeps the policy in their hands.

Tested with a mock client, per the llm package convention that no test makes a real call. A key exercises it against a provider; it is not needed to verify the command works.

title: merge reaches only the MCP surface
description:
registerMergeTool is in the MCP tool barrel. Neither the CLI nor the VS Code extension references mergeModels -- the narrowest reach of any shipped capability, one surface out of three.

Found by the cross-surface matrix in docs/unwired-capability-audit-2026-08-20.md.

Unlike review, merge needs no LLM and no key: it is pure core. `barwise merge <a> <b>` is cheap to add and testable offline, which makes it the easier half of the pair to settle.

Open question worth deciding first: is merge a modelling operation users want at the command line, or is it there for agent use through MCP specifically? If the latter, say so in the docs rather than leaving it looking like an oversight.

Closed by docs/specs/cli-surface-parity.spec.md. `barwise merge <base> <incoming>` ships with --output and --format yaml|json.

The open question -- is merge a modelling operation users want at the command line, or an agent affordance belonging to MCP alone -- resolved to the former. A merge only an agent can perform is a merge no human can review before it happens, and the CLI is where a human works a model into a state they are willing to commit. It is also the sibling of `barwise diff`, which already ships: the same comparison read in the other direction.

Two deliberate differences from the MCP tool, both recorded in the spec. The CLI does not write back to the base file -- defensible for an agent handed both paths, surprising for a command a human typed -- so the merged model goes to stdout and --output is how you ask for a file. And a merge producing structural errors writes nothing anywhere and exits 1, since a broken model on disk is worse than no model. Both have their own test.

VS Code still lacks merge; the capability matrix in CLAUDE.md now records that as deliberate, because merge in an editor wants a diff view and per-delta accept/reject, which is a UI feature rather than a wiring job.

title: CodeExtractionPrompt builds a prompt nothing sends to a model
description:
buildCodeExtractionPrompt is exported at packages/code-analysis/src/index.ts:31 and defined in prompt/CodeExtractionPrompt.ts:21. Its only other mention in any src/ tree is that export line. One test covers it. Nothing hands its output to a model.

docs/specs/prompt-optimization-harness.spec.md already scoped it out on exactly this ground: "dead code today (built, exported at src/index.ts:31, never sent to a model). It joins the harness when it gains a call site." Two months on it has not gained one.

The decision is not really about the code, it is about the design: was the code-analysis import path ever meant to run an LLM pass over assembled code context, or was that abandoned and this left behind? Answer that and the disposition follows -- give it a call site, or delete it and drop the export.

Carrying it is not free: it costs a test, it appears in the public export list where a reader will reasonably assume it is used, and it makes the next audit re-derive the same finding. Confirmed in docs/unwired-capability-audit-2026-08-20.md.

title: Few-shot demo rendering is built, tested, and never exercised
description:
PromptDemo, the loader validation in loadArtifact.ts:69-83, and renderDemos in prompt/artifacts/render.ts are implemented and tested. Both shipped artifacts declare demos: [], so no demo has ever rendered outside a unit test.

Nothing is broken and no action is needed yet. Filed so the gap is visible rather than discovered later: the DSPy optimizer lane is specified to export demos, and it will be the first thing to exercise this path in earnest.

What is unverified is behaviour under real content rather than fixture content -- specifically token budget. The extraction system prompt is already about 4,540 tokens; the harness spec flags demos carrying full JSON payloads as a grounding question for the exporter, possibly needing excerpt-truncation rules. That question stays open until something renders a real demo.

From docs/unwired-capability-audit-2026-08-20.md, which recommends leaving this alone until the optimizer lane needs it.
